contracts.name: TokenManager
contracts._rolesNote: HOK-3285: AMM pools are authorized by their ModelRegistry binding, not MINTER_ROLE, and DEPLOYER_ROLE gates nothing; the deployer's constructor-granted MINTER_ROLE and DEPLOYER_ROLE are revoked so no EOA keeps mint power. Governance (timelock, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) can grant MINTER_ROLE to an approved minter explicitly.

contracts.name: PoolProxyAdmin
contracts._ownerNote: HOK-3285: the single ProxyAdmin for every HokusaiAMM pool proxy. Owned by the timelock, so upgrades, upgradeAndCall and freezeUpgrades are all 48h-delayed and Safe-proposed. The contract refuses upgrades of paused or frozen pools and refuses changeProxyAdmin.

contracts.name: HokusaiAMM
contracts._checksNote: HOK-3285: each pool proxy must point at an approved implementation (the deploy-time default or one recorded in upgrades.approvedPoolImplementations after a timelocked upgrade), be administered by PoolProxyAdmin, be the ModelRegistry pool for its model (its only TokenManager mint/burn authority), and hold no TokenManager MINTER_ROLE.

contracts.name: DeltaVerifier
contracts._adminNote: DeltaVerifier DEFAULT_ADMIN intentionally stays at the 2-of-3 admin Safe (not the timelock) so mint-config posture changes (attesters, budget, genesis) are not 48h-delayed. Deployer is still revoked. Must match mainnet-launch-posture.json roleAudit.
contracts._submitterNote: SUBMITTER_ROLE goes to the backend relayer (RELAYER = governance.submitterRelayer / MAINNET_BACKEND_ADDRESS), NOT DEPLOYMENT_ROLE which resolves to the bootstrap deployer. Pairing this with SUBMITTER_ROLE in revokedFromDeployer makes the handoff grant the relayer and revoke the deployer in one pass — otherwise the handoff re-grants the deployer's bootstrap SUBMITTER (mainnet 2026-07-01 incident, required a post-handoff Safe cleanup).

contracts.name: UsageFeeRouter
contracts._depositorNote: HOK-3285: FEE_DEPOSITOR_ROLE goes to the backend service only; the deployer's bootstrap FEE_DEPOSITOR_ROLE is revoked (deploy-stack grants both).

contracts.name: DataContributionRegistry
contracts._adminNote: DataContributionRegistry DEFAULT_ADMIN intentionally stays at the admin Safe (not the timelock), consistent with DeltaVerifier and mainnet-launch-posture.json roleAudit. Deployer is still revoked.
contracts._recorderNote: RECORDER_ROLE is DeltaVerifier only (CONTRACT:DeltaVerifier), NOT DEPLOYMENT_ROLE which resolves to [deployer, DeltaVerifier]. With RECORDER_ROLE in revokedFromDeployer the handoff drops the deployer's bootstrap RECORDER while keeping DeltaVerifier's. Same class of bug as DeltaVerifier SUBMITTER (mainnet 2026-07-01). VERIFIER_ROLE stays DEPLOYMENT_ROLE (un-audited deployer-key leftover) — separate follow-up cleanup.
contracts._verifierNote: HOK-3285: VERIFIER_ROLE moves from the deployer key to the admin Safe (which already holds DEFAULT_ADMIN here); no off-chain service calls verify/rejectContribution today.

contracts.name: PurchaserWhitelist
contracts._rolesNote: HOK-3285: whitelist administration is a Safe operation (docs/purchaser-whitelist-operations.md); the deployer's bootstrap admin roles are revoked.

contracts.name: HokusaiToken
contracts._ownerNote: HOK-3318: per-model token Ownable owner is the 48h timelock. The token's only owner-power is setController, which can block every sell or route mints around TokenManager, so it carries the same notice as a pool upgrade. The factory makes the governor (admin Safe) the owner at creation; the Safe transfers it to the timelock before the handoff (scripts/governance/token-ownership-safe-bundle.js). The deployer never owns the tokens, so the handoff does not move them — ensureOwner flags non-deployer-owned contracts instead of reverting. HokusaiParams GOV_ROLE stays at the Safe.

contracts.name: HokusaiParams
contracts._rolesNote: HokusaiParams grants DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE to its deployer (the TokenManager) and GOV_ROLE to the governor (admin Safe) at construction, and TokenManager exposes no params role-management method — so neither role is the deployer's to move, and GOV_ROLE (the economic-param control: tokensPerDeltaOne etc.) is permanently held by the admin Safe by contract design (consistent with the H-1 token-owner decision: economic/control powers stay under the 2-of-3 Safe, not the timelock). The handoff therefore does not transfer params roles. Moving economic-param control to the timelock would require a TokenManager/params contract change (tracked follow-up).
